A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 13. It results from a power or time-unit error, not from $E/P$ with $E$ in $\text{J}$ and $P$ in $\text{W}$.

B.explanation: Matches $t = E/P$ where $E$ is the energy for 100 km and $P = IV = 2990 \text{ W}$.

C.explanation: This is the time to replace the full $200 \text{ MJ}$, not the $100 \text{ km}$ fraction actually used.

D.explanation: Too large. It corresponds to replacing more energy than was used for the 100 km drive.

hints: Notice that 150 km uses the full $200 \text{ MJ}$, but only 100 km was driven, so first find the fraction $100/150$ of the stored energy that must be replaced.
Recall charging power from the mains using $P = IV$ with $I = 13.0 \text{ A}$ and $V = 230 \text{ V}$, giving power in $\text{W}$ or $\text{J s}^{-1}$.
Connect energy and power with $t = E/P$, using $E$ in joules, then convert the time in seconds to hours by dividing by $3600$.
walkthrough: Find the energy used for the 100 km drive. Full range energy is $200 \text{ MJ}$ for 150 km, so $E = (100/150) \times 200 \text{ MJ} = 133.3 \text{ MJ} = 1.333 \times 10^8 \text{ J}$.
Find the charging power from the household supply. Use $P = IV$.
Substitute $I = 13.0 \text{ A}$ and $V = 230 \text{ V}$: $P = 13.0 \times 230 = 2990 \text{ W}$. This is $2990 \text{ J s}^{-1}$.
Use $E = Pt$ rearranged to $t = E/P$ for minimum time with 100% efficiency: $t = 1.333 \times 10^8 / 2990 = 4.46 \times 10^4 \text{ s}$.
Convert seconds to hours: $t = 4.46 \times 10^4 / 3600 = 12.4$ hours. This is option B.
